## Job Description

_**This role can sit anywhere in the US as long as it is near an Accenture Corporate Office.**_

Accenture helps the world's leading enterprises reinvent by building their digital core and unleashing the power of AI to create value at speed for organizations across industries. Our strategy is to be the reinvention partner of choice for our clients and lead in the safe, widespread adoption of AI, and to be the most client-focused, AI-enabled, great place to work in the world. We bring together the talent of our approximately 814,000 people with proprietary assets and platforms, deep process and industry expertise, and leading ecosystem relationships to deliver end-to-end solutions and measurable outcomes at scale. Through our Reinvention Services, we offer broad expertise across Cybersecurity, Digital Core, Finance, Industry and Enterprise, Song, Supply Chain and Engineering, and Talent, with advanced capabilities in AI and Data, Industry and Process, and Technology. We serve approximately 9,000 clients and generated approximately $74 billion in FY26 revenue. Visit us at [accenture.com](http://www.accenture.com/) .

**You are:**

You define how process transformation work gets done within your industry or function — setting the methodology, governing quality, and making sure every engagement reflects deep domain expertise as well as the right delivery standard. You manage and develop your team, coach senior specialists on what good looks like in your domain, and connect with technology and delivery partners to make sure the process and platform work fit together.  
  
You've made AX Design, the intersection of human, agent, and process part of the team's methodology — you've worked out how to apply it in your domain context, and you coach your team on what human+AI agent experience design looks like in practice.

**The work:**

Embed AI into future state design for clients as well as in ways of working for your full workstream using the appropriate AI tools and creating agents strategically to aid in deliverable creation.

* Define the process redesign standard for your industry or function — the method the team uses to assess domain forces, specify future-state processes, integrate AI, and design operating model changes — and govern its application across all engagements in your area.
* Determine the client facilitation approach: discovery workshop methodology, recommendation presentation standards, and approval governance.
* Define the benchmarking and transformation roadmap methodology the team applies.
* Determine how domain expertise and functional playbook methodology are applied consistently across the team's portfolio of engagements.
* Manage client stakeholder facilitation activities — discovery workshops, recommendation presentations, and day-to-day relationship management.
* Approve final process designs before client delivery.
* Manage and develop direct reports; coach senior specialists on process redesign, domain application, and senior leadership presentation.
* Connect with technology and delivery partners to make sure process design and platform work fit together on joint deliverables.
* Define how AX Design is embedded in the team's domain methodology — establishing the standard for how AI agent experiences are specified, reviewed, and validated within process transformation deliverables across all engagements.

**Travel Requirements:**

Travel is required for this role and could vary up to 75%

## Qualification

**Here's what you need:**

* Minimum 8 years of experience in process excellence, process redesign, or management consulting
* Minimum 2 years of deep industry expertise in at least one domain (e.g., Banking/Capital Markets, Insurance, Software and Platforms, Communications and Media, High Tech, Health, Public Service, Life Sciences, Consumer Goods Retail and Travel, Industrial, Energy, Utilities or Chemical and Natural Resources), with the ability to apply it to transformation methodology design
* Minimum 2 years of experience managing and developing team members
* Minimum 1 year of experience of building, evaluating, and scaling AI-enabled solutions into client work with the ability to explain how AI addresses business problems

**Set Yourself Apart:**

* Demonstrated ability to define and govern team methodology across a portfolio of client engagements
* Familiarity with process mining, digital twin, or AI-assisted design tools for process validation
* Experience contributing to business development, leadership proposal and facilitating client workshops
* Demonstrated ability to embed AI Design into team delivery standards — governing how AI agent experiences are specified and validated across process transformation engagements
* Understand AI partner ecosystem and help clients navigate complex technology choices
* Proven track record facilitating client workshops and presenting to senior leadership
* Strong executive communication and facilitation skills

  
Compensation at Accenture varies depending on a wide array of factors, which may include but are not limited to the specific office location, role, skill set, and level of experience. As required by local law, Accenture provides a reasonable range of compensation for roles that may be hired as set forth below.  
We anticipate this job posting will be posted until 11/28/2026.  
  
Accenture offers a market competitive suite of benefits including medical, dental, vision, life, and long-term disability coverage, a 401(k) plan, bonus opportunities, paid holidays, and paid time off. See more information on our benefits here:

### Job Description

Job Description

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on Plant Manager to lead site operations in an Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) environment. This leader will oversee manufacturing performance, operational strategy, workforce development, and financial execution while delivering improvements in quality, productivity, cost, delivery, and safety.

The ideal candidate brings progressive leadership experience in EMS, semiconductor, or OEM manufacturing, with a successful track record of building teams, scaling operations, and leading operational or technical turnarounds. The role requires a collaborative leader who can strengthen internal and customer relationships, support business growth, and deliver high-quality products on time and within budget.

Key Responsibilities  
Site Leadership and Strategic Execution

* Lead plant operations and establish strategies aligned with customer commitments, financial goals, and business objectives.
* Translate strategic priorities into operating plans, resource requirements, and measurable performance targets.
* Lead facility startups, capacity expansions, operational turnarounds, and organizational improvements as needed.
* Build and lead site-based teams and coordinate with remote, domestic, and international stakeholders.
* Communicate operational performance, business risks, investment needs, and improvement plans to executive leadership.

Manufacturing Operations

* Oversee daily production planning, scheduling, and execution in a low-to-medium-volume, high-mix manufacturing environment.
* Direct electronic, mechanical, and electromechanical production, including SMT, through-hole, testing, and final assembly.
* Optimize labor, equipment, materials, and capacity to achieve quality, delivery, productivity, and cost objectives.
* Identify production constraints and implement effective recovery plans.
* Maintain a visible manufacturing-floor presence through gemba walks and direct employee engagement.

Quality and Operational Excellence

* Drive improvements in first-pass yield, scrap, rework, throughput, and overall equipment effectiveness.
* Ensure adherence to first-article inspection requirements, SOPs, work instructions, and quality procedures.
* Partner with Quality and Engineering to resolve nonconformances, implement corrective actions, and verify sustained effectiveness.
* Apply Lean, Six Sigma, 5S, Kaizen, and structured problem-solving methods.
* Support audits, process validation, and compliance with applicable quality systems and customer requirements.

Leadership and Team Development

* Recruit, coach, and develop supervisors, managers, technicians, and production personnel.
* Establish clear expectations, accountability, succession plans, and employee development programs.
* Strengthen communication and consistent execution across departments and shifts.
* Foster a collaborative culture that balances employee engagement with operational discipline.
* Lead teams through growth, organizational change, and performance improvement.

Financial, Resource, and Engineering Management

* Manage plant operating budgets, labor utilization, overhead, and cost-reduction initiatives.
* Evaluate capital investments, equipment upgrades, and capacity requirements.
* Partner with Engineering and Maintenance to improve manufacturability, equipment reliability, and process capability.
* Coordinate with Supply Chain to address shortages, optimize inventory, and maintain production continuity.
* Support NPI, production transfers, and manufacturing readiness.

Customer Relationships and Business Growth

* Serve as a senior operational contact for customers regarding performance, capabilities, and delivery commitments.
* Partner with Sales and Business Development to assess new opportunities and align customer requirements with manufacturing capabilities.
* Support proposals, capability presentations, and operational assessments for prospective business.
* Build productive relationships with customers, suppliers, and internal stakeholders.
* Ensure growth commitments are supported by realistic capacity, cost, quality, and execution plans.

Safety and Compliance

* Promote a proactive safety culture and enforce established EHS policies.
* Ensure operations meet applicable regulatory, industry, and customer requirements.
* Support inspections, risk assessments, training, and corrective actions.

Qualifications

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience will be considered.
* Ten or more years of progressive manufacturing experience, including significant plant, site, or operations leadership responsibility.
* Direct experience in EMS, PCBA, semiconductor, or OEM manufacturing; Tier 1 industry experience preferred.
* Demonstrated success leading high-mix manufacturing operations and delivering measurable business results.
* Experience building teams and leading startups, expansions, high-growth operations, or operational and technical turnarounds.
* Strong knowledge of production planning, capacity management, manufacturing engineering, budgeting, and continuous improvement.
* Working knowledge of applicable quality systems and standards, such as ISO 9001, IPC-A-610, and J-STD-001.
* Experience with ERP/MRP systems; familiarity with MES and PLM systems preferred.
* Strong customer-facing communication, relationship management, and cross-functional leadership skills.
* Ability to balance strategic priorities with hands-on operational execution.

Preferred Qualifications

* Experience leading geographically distributed teams and collaborating across domestic and international operations.
* Exposure to strategic marketing, business development, or commercial planning within a manufacturing business.
* Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, or relevant IPC certification.
* Experience in regulated manufacturing environments.

Key Performance Measures

* On-time delivery and schedule attainment.
* First-pass yield, scrap, rework, and customer returns.
* Throughput, labor efficiency, and capacity utilization.
* Equipment availability and downtime.
* Operating costs and budget performance.
* Customer satisfaction and readiness to support business growth.
* Employee development, retention, and engagement.
* Safety performance.

Work Environment and Additional Requirements

This is an on-site leadership position requiring regular manufacturing-floor engagement and coordination across production shifts.

The position requires access to export-controlled technology and technical data. Applicants must meet the position’s stated ITAR eligibility requirements, subject to company screening.

## Job Description

The VP Manufacturing will provide strategic, operational, and technical leadership for the company’s manufacturing activities supporting late-stage clinical development, commercial readiness, and future commercial supply of the company’s lead biologic programs, including SAB‑142.  
  
This role is responsible for establishing scalable, compliant, and cost-effective manufacturing capabilities as the company advances SAB‑142 and other pipeline programs toward commercialization. The company is advancing a novel platform for the production of fully human, multi-targeted immunoglobulins (IgGs).  
  
The VP will lead manufacturing strategy and execution from late-stage clinical production through commercial launch readiness, with responsibility for manufacturing network strategy, CDMO management, technology transfer, scale-up, process validation, operational readiness, and reliable commercial supply. Experience with biologics manufacturing is required, and expertise in plasma fractionation, plasma-derived therapeutics, or analogous large-scale protein purification operations is desired.  
Working closely with Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Process Development, Clinical Operations, and Supply Chain, the VP will ensure that manufacturing operations meet global regulatory expectations, support clinical and commercial demand, and maintain a strong culture of safety, quality, compliance, and continuous improvement.  
  
**Duties and Responsibilities (include but are not limited to):**  
  
Manufacturing Strategy and Commercial Readiness

* Develop and execute the overall manufacturing strategy supporting late-stage clinical development, regulatory approval, and commercial launch readiness.
* Establish scalable manufacturing capabilities through an appropriate mix of internal capabilities and external CDMO partnerships.
* Lead manufacturing network planning, capacity planning, campaign readiness, and long-term supply resilience.
* Ensure manufacturing strategies support the unique requirements of complex immunoglobulin-based biologics, and high-purity protein products.

* Bachelor's degree in related field

* Computer knowledge
* Minimum of five years of supervisory experience

**The future of aerospace and defense starts here.  
**

Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from hypersonics to solid rocket motors, satellite maneuvering and launch. We design and deliver propulsion and defense systems that solve the most urgent and critical national security demands.

**Role Overview**

The Senior Director, Quality is the senior quality leader for Ursa Major. This leader is accountable for product quality, quality compliance, and the effectiveness of the Quality Management System across all sites and product lines, including solid rocket motors, hypersonic propulsion, in-space propulsion, and avionics. Reporting to the Chief Safety and Risk Officer, the Sr. Director serves as the company’s senior quality representative to DCMA, government customers, and prime contractors. They will build the program and customer-facing quality capability Ursa Major needs as it scales from development into rate production and operates as a public company.

This role leads the full quality organization, including quality control, inspection, metrology and calibration, quality systems, and product quality engineering, with full authority to shape its structure as the business grows. The ideal candidate knows what prime-level quality looks like and how to deliver it at startup speed, scaling rigor to risk rather than adding bureaucracy. This is a senior leadership role, but it is also a hands-on one: we expect this leader to roll up their sleeves, lead from the front, and work in the trenches alongside the team as we scale.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Quality Leadership & Strategy**

* Own Ursa Major’s quality strategy, objectives, budget, and organization, structuring and developing the quality team to support growth across all product lines and sites.
* Build a culture of quality where every function owns quality and builds it into design, sourcing, manufacturing, and delivery.
* Match quality rigor to program maturity: move at the speed development programs require while meeting the full expectations of mature defense and prime customer programs.

**Government & Prime Customer Quality**

* Serve as Ursa Major’s senior quality representative to DCMA, government customers, prime contractors, and certification bodies, building trust-based relationships with DCMA quality assurance representatives and customer quality organizations.
* Lead quality across Ursa Major’s business models: all-up-round deliveries directly to the U.S. government, SRM and propulsion deliveries as a supplier to defense primes, and in-space propulsion systems for satellite and spacecraft customers.
* Build an organization capable of reviewing proposals and contracts for quality requirements, including FAR/DFARS quality clauses and customer-specific requirements, and ensure they flow down and implemented across design, purchasing, manufacturing, inspection, and delivery.
* Own government source inspection, product acceptance, and customer audit readiness, including WAWF acceptance, government first article approval, and witnessed lot acceptance testing.
* Partner with material control to 3nsure effective control of government-furnished property and material under FAR 52.245-1, and support DCMA property management system reviews in partnership with Supply Chain and Contracts.
* Lead the company’s response to customer corrective action requests, audit findings, and quality escapes.

**Program Quality**

* Build Ursa Major’s program quality function, providing dedicated quality ownership for major programs and customers from contract award through delivery.
* Own contractual quality deliverables and commitments, including first article inspection reports, acceptance data packages, certificates of conformance, as-built records, and customer witness and hold points, and represent quality in program reviews and customer meetings.

**Quality Systems & Product Quality**

* Own the AS9100 Quality Management System and scale it across sites and product lines, including certification and audits, management review, nonconformance and Material Review Board, corrective action, and Nadcap accreditation of special processes where customers require it.
* Maintain effective controls for configuration, traceability, quality records, foreign object prevention, and counterfeit parts prevention, including GIDEP reporting.
* Partner with Engineering and Mission Assurance on design reviews, qualification, first article, and production readiness, and support a disciplined production rate ramp across solid rocket motors, hydrazine satellite propulsion systems, and potential future liquid-engine all-up rounds.
* In partnership with Safety, ensure quality controls fit energetics manufacturing, including propellant processing, cast-cure operations, and lot control and traceability of energetic materials.
* Ensure quality coverage for avionics and electronics, including electronics assembly workmanship and software and firmware quality, developing the team expertise needed as the avionics business grows.
* Shape supplier quality through influence rather than ownership: partner with Procurement, which owns supplier engineering, to set supplier quality requirements and flowdowns, weigh in on the selection and approval of critical suppliers, and drive resolution of supplier escapes.

**Authority & Public Company Governance**

* Hold authority to stop production, testing, acceptance, or shipment when product conformity, safety, or contractual compliance may be compromised, with an independent escalation path to the CEO and Business Unit President.
* Lead cost of poor quality reduction and continuous improvement: partner with Finance to accurately capture scrap, rework, and warranty costs in line with public company financial controls and use that data to drive measurable improvements.
* Other duties as assigned.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field.
* 10+ years of progressive quality experience in aerospace, defense, or similarly regulated manufacturing, including 5+ years in senior quality leadership building, scaling, and leading quality organizations.
* Direct, hands-on experience working with DCMA, including quality surveillance, government source inspection, and corrective action requests.
* Direct experience serving U.S. government and prime contractor customers, including contract quality requirements, FAR/DFARS quality clauses, requirement flowdowns, and customer audits.
* Demonstrated experience leading and sustaining an AS9100-certified Quality Management System.
* Experience leading quality through the transition from development into production and rate ramp.
* Track record of right-sizing quality rigor to risk, maintaining compliance and product integrity without slowing execution.
* Proven ability to build and sustain a strong culture of quality, where ownership of quality extends well beyond the quality organization.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with solid rocket motors, energetic materials, propellant processing, munitions, or tactical propulsion (strongly preferred).
* Public company experience (strongly preferred), including board-level reporting or supporting public company internal controls; experience through an IPO is a plus.
* Experience in both a traditional prime and a startup or non-traditional defense environment.
* Familiarity with avionics and electronics quality, such as electronics workmanship standards (IPC J-STD-001, IPC-A-610), ESD control, and software and firmware quality assurance.
* Master’s degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field.
* ASQ CMQ/OE, CQE, or CQA certification, or AS9100 lead auditor experience.

**Working Conditions / Physical Demands**

* Work performed in office, laboratory, and manufacturing environments, including hazardous and energetic operations areas that require personal protective equipment and adherence to explosives safety and site security protocols.
* Ability to sit or stand for extended periods and work on a computer for prolonged durations.
* Occasionally required to lift up to 25 pounds.
* Ability to travel up to 25% to Ursa Major sites, customers, suppliers, and government facilities.

  
Colorado law requires us to tell you the base compensation range of this role, which is $225,000 - $275,000, determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities. What we _can’t_ quantify for you are the exciting challenges, supportive team, and amazing culture we enjoy.

Classification: Full-time Exempt

## Power Generation Plant Manager

  
4406 Mentzer Road  
Convoy, OH 45832

The Power Generation Plant Manager directs the activities of [two gas turbine power plants](https://www.ohioec.org/generation-resources) located in Convoy, Ohio and Greenville, Ohio.  The Plant Manager ensures plant employees are in a safe, compliant, reliable, and economical manner including electric power production, maintenance, engineering, construction, accounting, procurement, materials management, human resources, public affairs, tax matters, and compliance with regulating agencies. Responsible for all activities and processes at the plant, and establishing and maintaining two-way communications with employees, managers, and the general public. Provides leadership and manages change by the development of a culture that promotes/supports teamwork, process improvement activities, employee development, and proper recognition and reward.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Plans, organizes, coordinates, directs, and controls plant operations, maintenance, engineering, and construction activities to ensure plant facilities operate safely, efficiently, and economically.
* Supports the safety process. Develops and maintains a safe working environment by providing proper tools, equipment, protective clothing, PPE and training. Establishes and enforces safe work behaviors. Participates in the setting of safety goals for an accident-free work environment. Communicates to employees the importance of a safe work environment on a daily basis. Investigates, reports, and tracks incidents/accidents including root cause analysis and corrective actions taken. Shares findings with management and employees.
* Develops long range plans (10 years) for maintenance and operational excellence, capital improvements, equipment availability, cultural transformation, and plant organizational succession planning.
* Directs long-range planning activities, including but not limited to maintenance management, materials management, QA/QC, human resources, accounting, predictive and preventative maintenance systems, and public relations.
* Develops short range plans and forecasts (3 years) in cooperation with engineering and maintenance personnel. Develops budgets, prepares variance reports, and controls expenditures to meet approved budgets.
* Directs the operation of plant activities to ensure compliance with all local, state, and federal laws and regulations and compliance with company policies and procedures.
* Directs engineering and related construction activities impacting the facility. Works with contract engineering/corporate engineering firms and contractors as needed to incorporate appropriate plant improvements.
* Directs the plant business processes, including but not limited to the following: accounting, procurement, materials management, human resources, environmental regulatory compliance, NERC regulatory compliance, safety, budgeting, contract management, outage planning/scheduling and public affairs.
* Participates in the formulation of company policies and procedures pertaining to plant operations and maintenance activities.
* Participates in the formulation of company policies and procedures for all business-related processes, including but not limited to the following: accounting, procurement, materials management, human resources, environmental regulatory compliance, NERC regulatory compliance, safety, budgeting, contract management, outage planning/scheduling and public affairs.
* Establishes and maintains strong working relationships with city, county, local, and other officials, as well as industrial leaders, and keeps appropriate individuals informed of actions, proposals, and plans affecting plant operations and activities.
* Performs other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

**Licenses and Certifications** : None required

* Minimum of ten (10) years of experience in power generation is preferred.
* Experience should include work in plant operations, maintenance, and performance areas.
* Experience should include business, financial and human resources administration.
* Minimum of ten (10) years of experience supervising others is required.

* **Reporting & Business Visibility:** Provide timely, accurate updates on purchase order status, production forecasts, late-order exposure, factory performance, and recovery plans, communicating material risks early with actionable recommendations.

You build strong relationships, lead teams with clear expectations, and thrive in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

10+ years of denim production experience, including 2-4+ years in a leadership role  
Deep knowledge of denim manufacturing, including factory operations, wash and finishing processes, and quality control

Track record of holding factories accountable for capacity, quality, and on-time delivery  
Experience protecting product costs by managing production changes, rework, and airfreight  
Strong reporting skills, with the ability to communicate order status, risks, and recovery plans clearly to leadership  
Experience leading and developing production teams  
Ability to partner cross-functionally and make sound decisions quickly in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment  
**

## Full Job Description

**Position Summary:** The Plant Manager is an on-site leader for BFI's Branchburg, NJ manufacturing facility and is accountable for plant leadership, partnering with functional area leaders, continuous improvement, managing and ensuring best practices are in place and upheld, along with establishing team goals, coaching and the development of the plant team. The Plant Manager owns manufacturing and warehouse operations and the plant's preventive maintenance program, and is responsible for safe, compliant, audit-ready, and efficient operations. The incumbent is responsible for plant safety and quality, including SQF food safety standards and audit readiness, in partnership with the Safety and Quality Assurance departments, which are accountable for those programs; drives productivity, performance, and continuous improvement; builds capabilities and team culture; manages the plant operating budget; partners with other department leaders on capital projects for equipment, facility, and plant enhancements; and maintains strong relationships with customers, suppliers, contractors, and customer and third-party auditors.

**Job Responsibilities:**

**_Plant Leadership and Team Development:_**

* Set clear plant and team goals aligned with company objectives, communicate them to the team, and track progress and results.
* Build a positive, can-do culture grounded in safety, quality, and accountability. Mentor and coach team members, explain the "why" behind decisions, and hold people accountable to clear expectations.
* Hire, onboard, and develop capable staff, including training, cross-training, and succession planning. Hold regular 1:1 feedback sessions and annual performance reviews so employees continue to grow in their roles.
* Address performance issues through coaching, performance improvement plans, and termination, when necessary, in partnership with HR and in compliance with labor laws and company policies.
* Lead regular plant communication initiatives and identify improvements to effectively reach an understanding of all colleagues, such as Tier 1, shift huddles and all-hands meetings, to share goals, audit and performance results, along with company updates. Monitor, direct, and guide Leads/Supervisors on how to effectively lead Tier 1 mtgs.
* Works across functions and partners with key leaders/departments to build for durability, contribute to business strategy and value creation.

**_Safety, Food Safety and Quality:_**

* Implement and enforce the plant safety program in compliance with OSHA requirements and company policies and procedures, including incident investigation, root-cause analysis, and corrective action.
* Uphold all food safety programs in accordance with SQF, GMP, and HACCP requirements and company policies and procedures.
* Partner with the Quality Assurance and Safety departments, which are accountable for the plant's food safety, quality, and safety programs, to ensure compliance with food safety and safety regulations and to put measures in place that reduce risk.
* Conduct regular plant inspections and GMP walkthroughs to verify compliance with safety, food safety, and quality standards.
* Create a culture of audit readiness in which every employee understands and follows food safety, quality, and safety requirements every shift, not just during audits, so the plant is prepared for announced or unannounced audits at any time. Reinforce this through shift huddles, floor walks, recognition, and accountability, in partnership with Quality Assurance.
* Support customer, certification (SQF, Kosher, Halal), and regulatory audits, and ensure corrective actions are completed on time.

**_Manufacturing, Warehouse, and Maintenance:_**

* Own manufacturing and warehouse operations, managing daily production and warehousing activities to meet safety, quality, output, and delivery goals, working closely with the Production Manager, Planning, and Quality.
* Coordinate with other managers on material procurement, production planning, inventory, quality, and workforce allocation to ensure effective execution.
* Ensure smooth scaling of new formulas from the lab to production and inventory accuracy for raw materials is maintained to acceptable standards.
* Track and report key performance indicators (e.g., safety incidents, yield, throughput, on-time delivery, inventory accuracy) and lead continuous improvement initiatives that increase efficiency and reduce waste.
* Serve as liaison between Operations and supporting teams such as Regulatory, Quality, Applications, and R&D, building close partnerships with department heads to troubleshoot, educate, and solve day-to-day operational issues.
* Resolve operational issues and conflicts promptly, implementing appropriate solutions and escalating when necessary.
* Own the plant preventive maintenance program, including PM schedules, work orders, spare parts, and maintenance records, to maximize equipment uptime and reliability and to support food safety and audit requirements.
* Track maintenance performance (e.g., PM compliance, downtime, mean time between failures) and drive root-cause analysis and corrective action on equipment failures.

**_Financial Management and Capital Projects:_**

* Partner with the VP, Operations and other department leaders on capital projects for equipment, facility, and plant enhancements, providing operational input on scope, timelines, and budgets and supporting compliance with specifications, building codes, and safety regulations.
* Request quotes and negotiate cost-effective contracts with contractors and vendors in line with BFI's standards of business conduct.
* Work with Finance to develop and manage the plant operating budget; control expenses, monitor financial performance, and identify and address variances or risks.
* Keep the VP, Operations informed of plant performance, risks, and priorities, and provide input on operational strategy.

**Qualifications:**

* Bilingual in English and Spanish
* Bachelor's degree in operations management, engineering, food science, supply chain, business administration, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience
* 7+ years of manufacturing operations experience in food, beverage, or ingredients, including 3+ years in a plant leadership role coaching and managing people
* Demonstrated leadership, coaching, collaborating with others, and effective verbal and written communication skills, along with the ability to build teamwork and accountability across the Branchburg team
* Working knowledge of OSHA safety regulations, Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), FDA regulations, and Food Safety (FSMA)
* Experience managing operating budgets, preventive maintenance programs, and inventory, and supporting capital projects
* Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to use data to drive results
* Excellent organizational and time management skills, with strong attention to detail and the ability to follow precise protocols
* Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, demanding environment
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint) for data management, reporting, presentations and communications
* Experience with ERP systems for production, inventory, and purchasing

**Preferred:**

* Background in GFSI (Global Food Safety Initiative) based food safety and production systems (FSSC 22000, SQF, etc.); SQF Practitioner certification a plus
* Knowledge of Kosher and Halal certification requirements
* Experience with Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen or other continuous improvement methods
* Experience with a computerized maintenance management system (CMMS)
* Experience with construction or facility projects and knowledge of building regulations

**Physical Demands:**

* While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit at a desk and to stand and walk on the production floor and in the warehouse for extended periods; use hands and fingers to operate a computer, phone, and other office and production equipment; and talk, hear, and reach. The employee may occasionally be required to balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, climb stairs, turn the head and torso, taste, or smell.
* Specific vision abilities include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.
* The employee may occasionally lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects weighing up to 50 pounds.

**Work Environment:**

* Work is performed both in an office environment and on the production floor and in the warehouse.
* Daily time on the production floor and in the warehouse, with exposure to odors, fumes, noise, moving equipment, and allergens (dairy and food colorings).
* The noise level ranges from moderate in the office to loud on the production floor.
* Occasional work outside normal business hours, including early mornings, evenings, or weekends, may be required to support production needs, audits, or emergencies.

**Personal Protective Equipment:**

* Non-slip steel-toed shoes are required on the Production Floor
* Hairnets and beard nets are required to be worn on the Production Floor
* Lab coats, uniforms, or coveralls are mandatory on the Production Floor

# Title: Director, Manufacturing Operations - Texas

Description: |**Summary:** |
| --- |
|The Director of Manufacturing Operations is the senior manufacturing operations leader for the Denton, Texas campus. **Plant 1** performs final assembly of make-to-order precision cooling units. **Plant 2** is a new, vertically integrated plant now in start-up, bringing component fabrication and finishing in-house, including an automated powder coat system.

This leader will bring both plants together as one site with one operating system, one leadership team, and one set of KPIs. The role leads Production, Planning & Materials (including Warehouse, Receiving, Material Handling, and Inventory), Maintenance, and Manufacturing Engineering, and partners closely with Quality, Supply Chain/Procurement, Engineering, Finance, HR, and PMO. We are looking for a hands-on, visible leader who turns strategy into measurable results on the shop floor and builds a team that can sustain them. |
|**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:** |
|**Safety, People & Culture**

* Build and lead a capable site leadership team; hire, onboard, coach, and evaluate managers, and develop succession depth for key roles.
* Set clear expectations and hold people accountable fairly and consistently, applying company policy (attendance, conduct, corrective action) in partnership with HR.
* Create a respectful, engaged workplace where concerns are raised early and problems are solved at the lowest effective level.
* Own site safety performance; drive hazard and near-miss reporting, root cause analysis, and timely closure of corrective actions.

**Production & Delivery**

* Deliver the annual production and revenue plan for the Denton campus, meeting customer commitments for on-time delivery and quality.
* Manage capacity, staffing, and shift structure across both plants to support growth with the right headcount and overhead structure.
* Synchronize Plant 2 component output with Plant 1 assembly demand so internal supply supports, rather than constrains, final assembly.

**Planning, Materials & Warehouse**

* Lead site planning, scheduling, receiving, warehousing, material handling, and inventory management to secure material availability, reduce lead times, and prevent shortages and stock-outs.
* Partner with corporate Supply Planning and Procurement on SAP master data, MRP, and supplier performance; assist with procurement guidance when needed (dotted line).
* Ensure supply chain policies and procedures are followed, and drive inventory accuracy and inventory turns targets.

**Maintenance & Manufacturing Engineering**

* Lead preventive and predictive maintenance programs to improve equipment uptime, with a focus on automated and capital-intensive equipment at Plant 2.
* Direct Manufacturing Engineering on process design, standard work, line balancing, work instructions, and new product introduction handoffs.
* Lead installation, commissioning, and acceptance (FAT/SAT) of capital equipment, and build and justify site capital plans.

**Plant 2 Start-Up & Site Integration**

* Lead Plant 2 through start-up and ramp-up to stable, rate-capable production, working with PMO and cross-functional partners on schedule, readiness, and staffing.
* Merge Plant 1 and Plant 2 into a single site organization with common roles, processes, meetings, and reporting.

**Operating System, Performance & Continuous Improvement**

* Deploy the STULZ Manufacturing Operating Model at the site: tiered daily meetings (Tier 1-3), a weekly site staff meeting, standard KPIs, and visual management.
* Translate annual strategy deployment (Hoshin Kanri / X-matrix) into site objectives, owners, and action plans, and review progress monthly.
* Provide accurate, timely, data-based reporting on safety, quality, delivery, productivity, cost, and inventory, and share results with the site team in a structured way.
* Lead a continuous improvement culture using Lean tools (5S, standard work, kaizen, problem solving); share best practices with other STULZ plants and adopt theirs.
* Manage the site budget and cost performance in partnership with Finance; understand plant financials and the drivers of margin.
* Support senior leadership in long- and short-range planning, policies, and objectives for U.S. manufacturing. |
|**What Success Looks Like (First 12 Months):** |
|* Plant 2 reaches stable production at planned rate, and Plant 1 and Plant 2 operate as one integrated site.
* Site leadership team is fully staffed, with clear roles and accountability.
* Tiered meetings and KPI reporting run consistently and drive daily decisions.
* Measurable improvement in safety, on-time delivery, productivity, and inventory accuracy versus baseline. |
|**Qualifications:** |
|**Required**

* Proven multi-department plant leadership covering production, materials/planning, and maintenance and/or manufacturing engineering.
* Experience in high-mix, low-volume, make-to-order manufacturing of engineered equipment (for example HVAC, electrical equipment, or industrial machinery).
* Track record of measurable results using Lean manufacturing and a structured operating system (tiered meetings, KPIs, standard work).
* Advanced working knowledge of ERP/MRP systems; SAP preferred.
* Strong analytical skills, including data analysis and trending in Excel; Power BI or similar is a plus.
* Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, bills of material, and specifications.

**Preferred**

* Experience leading a greenfield plant start-up, major expansion, or integration of multiple facilities.
* Exposure to fabrication and finishing processes (sheet metal, welding/brazing, powder coating) and to automated equipment.
* Experience with ISO 9001 quality systems.
* Experience in the data center, HVAC, or mission-critical equipment industry. |
|**Education/Experience:** |
|* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations/Supply Chain Management, Business, or a related field and 10+ years of manufacturing experience; Master’s degree or MBA a plus.
* 7+ years managing managers in a manufacturing environment, including multi-department or multi-shift responsibility. |
|**Certificates, Licenses, Registrations:** |
|* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt preferred.
* APICS/ASCM CPIM or CSCP preferred.
* OSHA 30 preferred. |
|**Leadership & Communication Skills:** |
|* Visible, hands-on leadership style with daily presence on the shop floor; leads through the team rather than doing the team’s work.
* Communicates clearly and respectfully with all levels, from operators to senior leadership, and delivers difficult information directly and diplomatically.
* Turns strategy into concrete plans, owners, and dates, and follows through to results.
* Shares data openly and in a structured, consistent format; open to feedback and committed to developing others.
* Ability to read and understand English instructions. |
|**Physical Requirements:** |
|This position involves a combination of office work and regular presence on the manufacturing floor. Responsibilities require moving throughout the facility, standing and walking during plant walkthroughs, using computers and other office equipment, reviewing operational information, and communicating with employees. The employee must be able to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation. |
|**Work Environment:** |
|Work is performed in office and manufacturing environments. Plant-floor activities may involve proximity to operating machinery, moving material-handling equipment, production noise, airborne dust or fumes, and varying temperatures, depending on the area and process. The employee must follow site safety procedures, use designated access routes, and wear required personal protective equipment when entering production or other designated areas. |

## Full Job Description

**Director of Manufacturing**

Do you thrive on leading manufacturing teams to deliver quality products on schedule?

Are you passionate about Lean Manufacturing and developing high-performing leaders?

Does working for a family-centric company with deep roots appeal to you?

Then Bedrock Truck Beds is right for you!

Department: Manufacturing / Operations | Primary Location: Shiner, Texas | Reports To: President

Director of Manufacturing Job Summary

The Director of Manufacturing is responsible for leading and optimizing manufacturing operations across the Shiner and Beeville facilities, overseeing flatbed production, the flatbed finishing line, and Manufacturing Engineering. This position is accountable for achieving production goals, improving operational efficiency, maintaining product quality, ensuring employee safety, controlling manufacturing costs, and delivering products on schedule.

The Director will lead manufacturing and engineering teams to establish consistent processes, improve product manufacturability, implement Lean Manufacturing principles, and drive continuous improvement across both facilities. This individual must be a hands-on, results-oriented leader with a strong background in metal fabrication, welding, assembly, finishing operations, manufacturing engineering, and multi-facility leadership.

**Director of Manufacturing Responsibilities:**

**Manufacturing Operations and Production**

* Direct manufacturing operations at both Shiner and Beeville facilities.
* Oversee flatbed fabrication, welding, assembly, finishing, and final inspection.
* Manage the flatbed finishing line to ensure proper workflow, production capacity, quality, and on-time completion.
* Establish production schedules and ensure manufacturing resources align with customer demand.
* Balance workloads, staffing, equipment, and production capacity between facilities.
* Standardize processes and best practices across both locations.
* Eliminate bottlenecks, downtime, rework, and inefficient use of labor and materials.

**Manufacturing Engineering Leadership**

* Direct and develop the Manufacturing Engineering team, establishing priorities, responsibilities, and performance expectations.
* Ensure Manufacturing Engineering supports production objectives, quality, cost reduction, and capacity improvements.
* Lead the development and implementation of standardized work instructions, process documentation, production layouts, and manufacturing methods.
* Drive improvements in fabrication, welding, assembly, tooling, fixtures, automation, and finishing processes.
* Partner with Design Engineering to improve design for manufacturability, simplify production, and reduce manufacturing costs.
* Lead engineering projects that improve labor productivity, product consistency, throughput, and equipment utilization.
* Evaluate and implement new manufacturing technologies, equipment, tooling, and automation.
* Establish engineering standards and ensure successful implementation of process changes across both facilities.
* Use data, time studies, and root-cause analysis to identify opportunities for measurable improvement.

**Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement**

* Lead the implementation and ongoing development of Lean Manufacturing practices across both facilities.
* Establish a culture of continuous improvement, waste elimination, and employee involvement.
* Apply Lean tools such as 6S, standard work, value stream mapping, visual management, root-cause analysis, and Kaizen events.
* Improve production flow, reduce work-in-process inventory, shorten lead times, and eliminate non-value-added activities.
* Identify and address bottlenecks throughout fabrication, welding, assembly, and finishing.
* Implement labor standards, cycle-time measurements, and productivity metrics where appropriate.
* Train and coach manufacturing leaders and employees in Lean principles and problem-solving methods.
* Track and verify improvements in productivity, quality, cost, and delivery performance.

**Leadership and Workforce Development**

* Lead, coach, and develop managers, production supervisors, and Manufacturing Engineering personnel.
* Establish clear expectations and accountability for performance across manufacturing and engineering.
* Build a culture focused on safety, quality, teamwork, ownership, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure adequate staffing, technical training, cross-training, and succession planning.
* Develop capable leaders who can manage daily operations while driving consistent results.

**Quality, Safety, and Compliance**

* Establish and maintain quality standards for flatbed manufacturing and finishing operations.
* Reduce defects, scrap, rework, warranty claims, and customer complaints.
* Ensure corrective actions address root causes and prevent recurring issues.
* Maintain compliance with applicable OSHA requirements and environmental regulations.
* Promote safe work practices in welding, cutting, grinding, material handling, finishing, and equipment operation.
* Hold manufacturing and engineering leaders accountable for safety and quality performance.

**Cost and Budget Management**

* Develop and manage manufacturing and Manufacturing Engineering budgets.
* Monitor labor productivity, material usage, scrap, rework, overtime, and manufacturing cost per unit.
* Lead cost-reduction initiatives without compromising safety or product quality.
* Evaluate capital investments in equipment, tooling, automation, and facility improvements.
* Partner with Purchasing and other departments to improve operating performance and reduce material cost.

**Materials, Maintenance, and Supply Chain Coordination**

* Coordinate with Purchasing and Planning to ensure material availability.
* Align production schedules with inventory, labor, equipment, and shipping capacity.
* Ensure preventive maintenance supports equipment reliability and minimizes downtime.
* Coordinate finished-product flow through shipping.

**Performance Management and Reporting**

* Establish and maintain consistent KPIs for both facilities and Manufacturing Engineering.
* Conduct regular reviews of safety, quality, production, delivery, cost, and engineering performance.
* Report results, risks, and improvement initiatives to executive leadership.
* Use data-driven decision-making to prioritize projects and measure results.
* Ensure accountability for improvement initiatives and expected business outcomes.
* All other duties as assigned by management.

**Director of Manufacturing Skills and Competencies**

* Strong analytical, communication, leadership, and problem-solving skills.
* Proficiency with ERP systems, production reporting, and Microsoft Office or comparable tools.

**Director of Manufacturing Qualifications**

* 7–10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, preferably in metal fabrication, welding, assembly, or industrial manufacturing.
* Demonstrated experience implementing Lean Manufacturing principles and delivering measurable improvements in productivity, quality, cost, and lead time.
* Experience leading Manufacturing Engineering, production operations, and multiple manufacturing departments or facilities.
* Strong understanding of fabrication, welding, assembly, finishing, production scheduling, and manufacturing processes.
* Proven ability to improve manufacturing flow, eliminate waste, and increase labor productivity.
* Experience with Lean tools such as 6S, Kaizen, value stream mapping, standard work, visual management, and root-cause analysis.
* Experience leading and developing managers, production supervisors, manufacturing engineers, and hourly employees.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing process development, tooling, fixtures, automation, and design for manufacturability.
* Experience managing budgets, capital projects, production capacity, and manufacturing cost controls.
* Ability to travel occasionally between Shiner and Beeville (approximately 90% Shiner / 10% Beeville).

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
* Experience in truck equipment, commercial vehicle upfitting, agricultural equipment, or heavy metal fabrication.
* Lean certification or formal Lean training, such as Lean Six Sigma, is a plus.

**Physical Requirements**

Work may involve walking and standing in manufacturing areas and using required personal protective equipment.

**Work Environment**

Manufacturing and office environments, with regular presence on production floors. Primary location is Shiner, with occasional visits to Beeville.
